entries.title: Your electronics workbench
entries.subtitle: From one LED to a software bus

blocks.text: Welcome to the 8052 laboratory
Follow a practical route: make materials and a board, name GPIO pins, wire an LED, flash a program, then add buttons, displays and sensors. Every module has its own entry in Modules.
New here? Start with First LED, then Button controls LED. Try the OLED or thermometer afterwards. Add one device at a time so faults are easy to isolate.
How to use this book

Use the four tabs for categories. Search covers titles, prose, terminals and addresses throughout the book. Scroll over the index to move entries, or over the page to turn pages. Arrow keys turn pages, Ctrl+F focuses search, and Home returns here.

Star the current entry and use Bookmarks to filter favorites. Recipe cards use the current world recipes. Hover items for their tooltips and click documented items to open their entries. The Copy button copies the entire code block.

entries.title: Materials to microchips
entries.subtitle: Ore, wafers and circuit boards

blocks.text: Two sources of raw silicon

Find silicon ore in newly generated Overworld chunks at Y=-56 to 40. Use a stone pickaxe or better. Fortune increases raw drops and Silk Touch preserves the ore. Existing chunks need newly explored terrain.
For an alternative, surround charcoal with four sand blocks. Raw silicon and both ore variants can be refined into wafers.
Make the PCB and MCU
Copper, clay and redstone produce two circuit boards. Wafers are the basis of chips and oscillators. Package an STC89C52RC, then combine it with a crystal and PCB to make the minimum system.
Picking up key materials unlocks vanilla recipe-book entries. Handbook cards also reflect recipe changes made by data packs.
Next: assemble the system board >

entries.title: First LED
entries.subtitle: One board, one cable, one output

blocks.text: Goal and materials
Goal: light an LED using your own 8052 program. Bring a system board, LED module, wire coil and HEX file. A new board includes an 11.0592 MHz crystal; all face terminals start unassigned.
1 · Name a terminal
Place the board, right-click it and open Six-face terminals. Choose an accessible face, edit G1, add label LED with kind GPIO and physical pin P1.0. Save and Apply.
2 · Connect the lamp
Place the LED nearby. Use the coil on the configured board group, then on the LED. A single terminal matches automatically. The finished cable stays visible after putting the coil away.
3 · Flash a minimal program
Compile this program in Keil C51 with HEX output enabled. Enter the HEX path on Programming and debugging, or drop the HEX file there. Flash it, then press Run.
GPIO 1 lights the LED and 0 turns it off. Stop pauses the CPU and the lamp keeps the port level. Board and connector redstone outputs return to zero when stopped.
Next experiment: button controls LED >
Lamp still dark? Troubleshoot it >

entries.title: Flashing and first run
entries.subtitle: HEX is firmware; C is source

blocks.text: Prepare firmware in Keil

Create an 8051/C51 project for a compatible STC89C52 target. Start with the SMALL memory model and 12T timing. Enable Create HEX File under Output, then build and select the generated .hex. C, OBJ and A51 files are not flashable HEX images.
Panel workflow

Bundled examples are selected by default. Open the example list, choose a program, check wiring and clock, then Flash HEX and Run. All eight ship inside the mod; no download or path is needed. Switch to Local HEX for your Keil program, use the file-picker button or drop a file. The top-right X closes the board screen.

rows: Validate, replace firmware and reset CPU

blocks.text: Paths refer to files on the client computer. Relative paths start at the game instance directory. Flashing sends firmware bytes to the server; the server does not open that local path.
Stop and check configuration after changing wiring, the crystal or a driver. Flashing and reset keep wiring; CPU reset also preserves the independent OLED framebuffer.
If HEX validation fails

Check that the file is complete, has an EOF record and valid checksums, and stays within the 8 KiB CODE region 0000H–1FFFH. Invalid or out-of-range HEX does not replace existing firmware. The text payload limit is 128 KiB.
Check wiring with bundled HEX examples >

entries.title: Minimum system board
entries.subtitle: Firmware, wiring and clock

blocks.text: The STC89C52RC, crystal, copper and PCB form a minimum system. New boards include an 11.0592 MHz oscillator. Each board owns independent firmware, CPU, RAM, GPIO and terminal groups.
Three working pages

rows: Flash, run, stop, reset and step
World faces, G1–G4, labels and physical pins
Remote devices, pins, offline paths and conflicts

blocks.text: The top-right crystal socket uses inventory items. Removing or replacing the oscillator pauses the CPU; Run resumes it after installation. Board faces use world directions, independent of your viewpoint. Check them with the compass.
Saving and breaking

CPU state, RAM, firmware and wiring persist with the board. Unloaded chunks pause the CPU without offline catch-up. Breaking a board refunds its cables, but the dropped board loses firmware and RAM; its crystal is retained.
A comparator reads the running state: 15 while running and 0 while stopped. Use it as a run indicator without consuming a GPIO.
Configure six-face terminal groups >
MCU memory regions >

entries.title: Faces and pin labels
entries.subtitle: Define the interface before wiring

blocks.text: Every world face has four independent groups, G1–G4. Name each group and add multiple pins. A label such as SDA, SCL, DQ or LED identifies the module interface. A physical pin such as P1.6 identifies the MCU port bit used by your program.
Adding and applying

Open pin management for a face, choose a group and set its name. Add a label, kind and physical channel for each pin. Labels are case-insensitive and unique within a group, as are physical channels. Apply saves all four groups on that face.

One face can use G1 for an OLED, G2 for another I²C bus, G3 for a thermometer and G4 for an LED. Groups may reuse labels, but choose independent GPIO where separate buses are intended. Renaming keeps physical wiring; removing or changing connected physical pins requires pairing again.

GPIO handles both input and output without a direction selector. Before reading an external input, set its latch bit to 1 to release it. Clearing a group refunds its cables. Use an external PCF8591 for analog input and output.
Analog conversion and complete experiment >
Connect the interface with a cable >

entries.title: Analog signals and external chips
entries.subtitle: Digital GPIO; external PCF8591 ADC / DAC

blocks.text: The STC89C52RC has no ADC / DAC

Since 1.10.0, board virtual ADC and DAC are removed. Board terminals bind P0.0–P3.7 GPIO for both input and output, without a digital direction selector. Use an external PCF8591 to read redstone strength or emit analog redstone 0–15.

rows: Input: zero low, nonzero high; output: 0 or 15
North, east, south, west; redstone strength times 17 gives 0–255
Upward output 0–15; enable with control bit 6

blocks.text: Experiment: PCF8591 input to output

Bring a board, PCF8591, coil, variable redstone source and output device. On any board face and G1–G4 group add GPIO SDA=P1.6 and SCL=P1.7, Apply, then wire to PCF8591. Default seven-bit address is 48H: write byte 90H and read byte 91H.

Put the redstone source north of PCF8591 for AIN0 and the target above it for AOUT. Flash examples/pcf8591_mirror.hex and Run. Inputs 0, 7 and 15 should produce the same outputs. The default crystal works; firmware uses GPIO software I²C.
Keil C51 transaction sequence

The following matches examples/pcf8591_mirror.c and requires examples/i2c_soft.h. Discard and ACK the previous conversion, then read and NACK the fresh value. Control 40H selects single-ended AIN0 and enables AOUT.

PCF8591 DAC bytes range 0–255 and map to redstone using rounded (value*15+127)/255. Send 170 instead of sample for strength 10. Clear control bit 6 to disable output. Converter state belongs to the module, not the board. Stopping the MCU sends no further commands, so AOUT holds its last value; write zero or disable it before stopping if needed.

PCF8591 and the environment sensor both default to 48H. On one SDA/SCL bus, sneak-use PCF8591 to select 49H and change firmware address bytes to 92H/93H, or use a separate GPIO bus. OLED defaults to 3CH and may share the bus.
Memory addresses and old saves

rows: Ordinary XDATA RAM; former ADC window released
Ordinary XDATA RAM; former DAC window released
PCF8591 I²C bus addresses, not memory addresses

blocks.text: Virtual ADC/DAC were removed in 1.10.0 and the OLED MOVX bridge in 1.10.1. All 64 KiB XDATA is now ordinary XRAM with no peripheral windows. External PCF8591 and OLED use GPIO software I²C and reserve no MCU memory addresses. Variables or framebuffers allocated by firmware still consume their chosen MCU memory.

Old saves discard ADC/DAC terminals but preserve GPIO names, channels, groups and wire IDs. Boards with retired analog pins pause while retaining firmware and CPU/RAM. Cut and reconnect invalid analog pairs; ADC/DAC is never silently mapped to GPIO. Update adc_mirror.hex or firmware accessing the retired windows before running again.
PCF8591 controls and channel modes >
XDATA versus I²C addresses >

entries.title: MPU6050 inertial sensor
entries.subtitle: Raw acceleration and angular rate; estimate attitude in firmware

blocks.text: Independent software-I²C peripheral. Address defaults to 68H. Sneak-use with an empty hand toggles AD0 between 68H/69H and saves it. WHO_AM_I remains 68H. Share named SDA/SCL wires with the OLED and altimeter on the same GPIO pair.

Works alone: stationary blocks report +1 g on Z and zero gyro. On Sable bodies it samples actual three-axis rate and acceleration. Create/Aeronautics are optional. It exposes no hidden Euler angles and runs no Java attitude solver or PID.
Axes and format

Local axes: X east, Y north, Z up, forming a right-handed frame. All raw signed 16-bit measurements are big-endian, two’s complement. Each read transaction latches a frame. Gravity and translational acceleration affect measurements; acceleration is not itself an angle.

rows: Sample divider / CONFIG; retained for readback
Interrupt-enable readback; data-ready clears on reading 3AH
AX, AY, AZ; high byte first
GX, GY, GZ; high byte first

blocks.text:
write(0x68,0x6B,0x00); // wake
write(0x68,0x1B,0x00); // 250 deg/s
write(0x68,0x1C,0x00); // 2 g
read(0x68,0x3B,14);   // accel, temperature, gyro

This simulates the common raw-register subset. Values update once per game tick, normally 20 Hz. Divider and CONFIG retain values but generate no 1 kHz subsampling or hardware DLPF. FIFO, DMP, auxiliary-master I²C, interrupt pins, self-test and real thermal noise are not implemented. Temperature is currently fixed at 25 Celsius.
Copy the complete MPU6050 driver >

Select mpu6050_oled.hex, install a 12 MHz crystal and connect OLED 3CH on P1.6 SDA/P1.7 SCL. It continuously displays this module's readings with disconnect errors and recovery. See Example firmware index for wiring, units and source dependencies.

entries.title: ALT-01 height sensor
entries.subtitle: World altitude, relative height and vertical speed

blocks.text: A mod-defined altimeter, not a BMP280 emulation. Seven-bit address 76H, write ECH/read EDH. Works alone using the module center’s world Y. On Sable bodies it follows actual physics position and vertical speed. Height is independent of redstone and does not require ground beneath.

rows: bit0 valid, bit1 on a moving body
Write A5H to capture the current zero

blocks.text: Altimeter fields are little-endian, unlike the MPU6050. The zero reference persists and applications can recapture it as needed. Players implement altitude control in firmware.

write(0x76,0x12,0xA5); // capture takeoff zero
read(0x76,0x0E,4);     // signed little-endian cm
Copy the complete altimeter driver >

entries.title: Multi-channel motor interface
entries.subtitle: Six adjacent faces, independent signed RPM

blocks.text: Each interface controls only Create creative motors directly touching its six faces. It never looks up remote motors relative to the board. Channels 0–5 are down, up, north, south, west, east, each accepting signed -256 to +256 RPM. Without Create, I²C still works and the detected mask is zero; no mechanical power is created.

Default address 60H. While SAFE, sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle 60H through 67H. The address persists. Eight different addresses on one SDA/SCL pair provide 48 channels. Another GPIO pair can form a separate bus. Duplicate addresses are reported as conflicts in Wiring.

rows: Read bit0 armed; write A5H to arm, other values to stop
Six staged signed little-endian RPM words
Write A5H: atomically commit six channels and refresh watchdog

blocks.text: Firmware must keep committing fresh commands. More than four ticks without activity, disconnection, stopped MCU or reload disarms and zeros adjacent motor commands. Write A5H again to rearm. Arming gives a short initial commit grace period. Existing rotor inertia remains.
Firmware chooses channels and output values. The interface supports independently controlled motors in arbitrary layouts.
Copy the complete motor interface driver >

entries.title: Cables and junctions
entries.subtitle: Click two endpoints; match labels

blocks.text: Connect two positions

Use the coil on a board group, then a module. Aim at the correct G1–G4 socket; the HUD shows the group name and pins. Single terminals match directly. Multiple terminals match by label, or open a pairing screen if the match is ambiguous.
A cable can carry several signals: SDA and SCL for an OLED, or all eight display segments. Button panels instead expose an independent endpoint for every key, with one cable per key.
Distance, branches and routing

Each segment spans at most 32 blocks within one dimension. Material cost is rounded up by distance. Junction posts extend, turn and branch cables. An empty post inherits the first connected terminal labels. Route around solid obstacles.
Each connected terminal network has one controlling board group. Do not join two board outputs directly. Devices sharing an address can be placed on separate GPIO buses.
Disconnecting and offline devices

Sneak-use the coil to cancel a selection. Use cutters on a visible cable, or break an endpoint to refund attached cables. Both endpoints and intermediate posts must be loaded. Offline routes remain visible in the wiring status for diagnosis.
Junction branching rules >
Share an I²C bus between devices >

entries.title: Crystals and timing
entries.subtitle: Software delays depend on frequency

blocks.text: Choose 6, 11.0592, 12, 22.1184 or 24 MHz. Open the top-right board socket and move crystals from inventory. Changes pause execution while retaining CPU and RAM; Run resumes it.

The bundled DS18B20 HEX specifically uses 12 MHz/12T. Do not substitute the default 11.0592 MHz crystal. OLED GPIO transfers do not strictly validate bus speed, though your software delays still change.
The default cycle budget is oscillator frequency divided by 240 per game tick, matching 12T at 20 TPS. Lower server TPS slows simulated progress. Unloaded chunks do not execute firmware.
Drive the thermometer at the right frequency >

entries.title: Keil projects and GPIO
entries.subtitle: Use C51 or assembly

blocks.text: Recommended starting point

Use an 8051/C51 toolchain with code limited to 8 KiB. Start with the SMALL model. REG52.H provides common SFR and bit definitions. Enable HEX output and flash it into the board. Your computer compiles C; the game executes machine code.
Bit and byte port access

This maps an active-low key to an active-high LED. Write 1 to KEY before reading to release its port. Writing 0 keeps it low. P1=0x3F writes all eight bits together and is useful for a segment display.
Analog signals use external chips
PCF8591 experiment and complete C51 program >

The board provides no ADC/DAC. Former windows F000H–F007H and F010H–F017H are ordinary XDATA RAM. Use external PCF8591 software I²C for conversions, control words and DAC bytes. Verify pcf8591_mirror.hex first, then edit its C source.
Bundled HEX examples are equivalent hand-assembled programs generated by project scripts. The C sources are provided for editing in Keil; software delay lengths may vary with compiler optimization.
Common registers at a glance >

entries.title: Debugging the board
entries.subtitle: PC, opcodes and stepping

blocks.text: Programming and debugging shows the opcode and disassembly at the current PC, plus three sequential instructions. After a branch, the preview remains sequential; the CPU determines the actual next instruction.
A repeatable debugging process

Stop and note the PC. Check the crystal and wiring, then reset. Step through the program and inspect whether port writes reach the intended pins. Verify a minimal output before adding buttons, sensors and control loops.

rows: Run state, installed crystal and CPU fault
Intentional waits or an unreleased input
Pin mapping, label, polarity and connector mode
Flash and run the correct file again

blocks.text: The virtual UART serves as a console: writing SBUF immediately appends a character and sets TI. Input needs receiver enable and RI handling in firmware. The console keeps the last 512 characters and does not simulate physical serial wiring.
A5H is reserved and stops execution with a fault. If execution enters erased code or jumps unexpectedly, check code limits and branch targets before resetting.
Full troubleshooting checklist >

entries.title: Button panel
entries.subtitle: Up to nine independent keys

blocks.text: Sneak-use with an empty hand, or use a blank area, to configure 1–9 keys. Every key has its own label. The first is KEY, followed by KEY2–KEY9; rename them START, STOP or other meaningful labels.

Add matching GPIO labels on the board. Use the coil on the board group and each individual key. Every key needs its own cable, and several keys can share a configured group. Renaming keeps wiring; shrinking the panel refunds cables for removed keys.
Pressed is 0; released is 1

Using a key pulls its signal low for 10 ticks, then releases it automatically. Release the corresponding MCU latch first. This complete program lights an LED while the key is active; wire the key and lamp separately as shown.
Keys hold a logical low for game ticks; mechanical contact bounce is not simulated. Removing an active key releases it rather than leaving a permanently low input.
Appendix: copy complete .h / .c >

entries.title: LED panel
entries.subtitle: Up to 3x3, individual colors and wires

blocks.text: Right-click empty-handed to configure 1–9 lamps at stable 3x3 positions. Select a lamp, enter its GPIO label and choose a 16-color preset or six-digit RGB hex such as FF4040. Apply saves; cancel/close does not. Every lamp is active-high.
Use adjacent G1 named LED, or wire any remote group. Changing to P2.3 requires updating both the board mapping and the sbit declaration.
The LED is an active-high logic indicator. Use a redstone connector to turn GPIO levels into signals for machines.
Send a logic signal to machinery >
Wire each lamp independently

Defaults are LED and LED2–LED9. Bind GPIO labels on the board, then use the coil on a board terminal and a particular lamp. Each has its own visible cable; this is not a serial RGB strip. Nine lamps may use P0.0–P0.7 and P1.0; split them across two groups to stay within eight cables per endpoint. No MCU registers or addresses were added.

Indices and positions remain stable. Rename/recolor preserves wires; shrinking removes and refunds only excess-lamp wires. Colors, names and count persist, with live states synchronized to clients. Reload clears stale input states. Legacy single lamps load with the default green color and LED label, keeping the original wire.

entries.title: Eight-segment display
entries.subtitle: Seven bars and a decimal point

blocks.text: One digit consists of segments A–G and decimal point DP. Common power and current limiting are built in, so only eight signal terminals are needed. One multi-signal cable can pair all eight.
Polarity and bit order

Default common cathode lights on 1. Sneak-use switches to common anode, which lights on 0. Bits 0–7 map to A B C D E F G DP. Invert the whole code byte for common anode. Missing pins or disconnected wiring blank both modes.

seven_segment_counter.hex counts 0–9 at the default crystal frequency, lighting DP on odd digits, about every 0.55 seconds. IDATA 30H stores the digit and 31H the code. Polarity persists with the module.
Find the counter example >
Appendix: copy complete .h / .c >

entries.title: SSD1306 OLED
entries.subtitle: 0.96 inch, 128×64 framebuffer

blocks.text: The separate OLED block owns an SSD1306 controller and 1024-byte framebuffer. Its 7-bit I²C address is 3CH and write byte is 78H. Right-click opens a magnified display, independently of the board. Both views use the same pixels.
Start with readable text
Map SDA=P1.6 and SCL=P1.7, then run i2c_oled_hello.hex. Expect EMBEDDED DEV, STC89C52, HELLO MINECRAFT and I2C 0X3C. oled_pattern.hex intentionally displays diagnostic stripes rather than text.
Commands and display bytes

rows: AE off / AF on / A6 normal / A7 inverse

blocks.text: RAM is page-organized: each byte holds eight vertical pixels of one column, with bit 0 at the page top. Pixel (x,y) uses offset (y>>3)*128+x and mask 1<<(y&7). Initialize addressing before sending glyph data.
The OLED saves its own RAM and display settings. CPU reset does not clear it. Clear residual graphics in firmware. For a blank display, first check AF display-on, SDA/SCL mapping and the address.

Replace legacy MOVX firmware with current software-I2C examples. Use i2c_oled_hello.hex for text and oled_pattern.hex for stripes. Duplicate oled_hello.hex was removed from the catalog; existing flashed boards keep their firmware.
I²C starts, ACKs and shared buses >
Appendix: copy complete .h / .c >

entries.title: DS1302 clock
entries.subtitle: Three wires, BCD calendar and RAM

blocks.text: DS1302 uses CE, SCLK and IO, not I²C. Raise CE to begin and lower it to commit and finish. Commands and data are LSB first. Rising edges capture writes; falling edges update read output. Release IO before reading.
Initialize the clock
Write 00H to 8EH to disable write protection, then write a BCD calendar. Seconds bit 7, CH, halts at 1 and runs at 0. BCD 23 is 23H, not decimal 23 encoded as 17H. Encode tens times 16 plus units.
For seconds, send 81H, release IO and read eight bits. Burst reads capture a consistent calendar snapshot instead of mixing fields across a second boundary. The 31-byte RAM can hold small parameters.

The clock follows game ticks rather than the computer wall clock. Calendar, halt state, write protection and RAM persist with the module. Firmware stops while its board is unloaded; clock progress follows world time.
Appendix: copy complete .h / .c >

entries.title: PCF8591 ADC / DAC
entries.subtitle: External I²C converter, with no MCU memory window

blocks.text: PCF8591 uses SDA/SCL, four 8-bit ADCs and one DAC at 7-bit addresses 48H–4FH, reserving no MCU XDATA or SFR. STC89C52 has no internal ADC/DAC, and board virtual converters were removed in 1.10.0. Use external chips for analog signals.
Complete ADC to DAC experiment and C51 program >
The default 7-bit address is 48H: write byte 90H and read byte 91H. Sneak-use cycles addresses 48H–4FH. AIN0–AIN3 sample world north, east, south and west; AOUT drives redstone upward.
Redstone input 0–15 maps to 0–255 by multiplying by 17. The DAC maps 0–255 back to 0–15 redstone. Control this chip through GPIO software I²C transactions, rather than board MOVX addresses.
Read AIN2
START, send 90H and control 02H. Repeated START, send 91H. Read and discard the first byte with ACK. The second byte is the current sample; finish with NACK and STOP.
The first read byte is the previous conversion, not the current input. Sending control 40H followed by a DAC byte enables and sets analog output.
The environment sensor also defaults to 48H. On one SDA/SCL bus, move the converter to 49H, or use independent GPIO buses.
Address conflicts and repeated START >

entries.title: DS18B20 thermometer
entries.subtitle: Touch a machine and read DQ

blocks.text: Place the probe against the target block; it samples only its contacted neighbor. Bind GPIO label DQ in any board group and wire it to the probe. Right-click for temperature, source and range information.
Use the supplied example first
Install 12 MHz, DQ=P1.2 and OLED on P1.6/P1.7, then run ds18b20_read.hex. Each pass waits at least 800 ms, validates scratchpad CRC, displays signed temperature and retries continuously.
Combine the first two bytes as a signed little-endian 16-bit value and divide by 16 for Celsius. Preserve the sign for negative temperatures. The last byte is a Dallas CRC8.
85 °C often means conversion has not completed. All FFH often means DQ is disconnected, not released, or not reset correctly. Check the 12 MHz crystal before investigating 1-Wire timing.

entries.title: Environment sensor
entries.subtitle: Redstone, light and day progress

blocks.text: The 7-bit address is 48H, with write 90H and read 91H. Write a register number, then switch to reading with a repeated START. Consecutive reads increment the register. Right-click to inspect current samples.
i2c_sensor.hex now shows all four environmental readings on OLED, retaining the P1.2 nonzero indicator. Install 12 MHz and share P1.6/P1.7 with sensor and display.
Its default address matches the PCF8591. Move the converter to 49H when sharing a bus. The OLED at 3CH does not conflict.

entries.title: Redstone connector
entries.subtitle: Connect MCU logic to machinery

blocks.text: Place a connector beside a device and wire it to the board. Right-click to select input or output and the redstone-facing side. Direction is relative to the MCU: machine signals enter as input; MCU control signals leave as output.
Read analog strength

The redstone connector input provides digital low/high only; there is no board ADC. To distinguish strengths 0–15, use PCF8591: SDA=P1.6, SCL=P1.7, default address 48H. Apply redstone to north AIN0 and run pcf8591_mirror.hex; upward AOUT mirrors its strength.
PCF8591 addresses, control word and transactions >

Use it for Create clutches, redstone links, and other mods accepting redstone control. The target mod determines machine behavior. Pulses shorter than one game tick may not appear in the redstone world.
Stopping the board or cutting a cable clears redstone output. Beside a legacy adjacent board, normal use may open the board; sneak-use opens connector settings.
Appendix: copy complete .h / .c >

entries.title: Junction post
entries.subtitle: Corners, extensions and branches

blocks.text: First connect a board group to an empty post so it inherits those labels. Wire the post to modules or further posts. Branches carry the mapped signals; they do not create extra MCU pins.
Useful circuits
A shared SDA/SCL pair can branch to an OLED, PCF8591 and environment sensor if addresses are unique. Several LEDs can branch from one GPIO and follow the same level.

A connected network has one controlling board group. Posts must be loaded to pass signals. Cutting the trunk disconnects downstream devices. Each post accepts up to eight segments and a network up to 64 endpoints.
Coil and cutter operations >

entries.title: Compass and world faces
entries.subtitle: Orient yourself before wiring

blocks.text: The compass points to world north. Use it to show your current heading in the action bar. Board terminals also show player direction. Your visual left and right change with position; configured world faces do not.
For adjacent connections, configure G1 on the board face touching the module. A module east of the board uses its east face. For remote groups on one face, aim at each group socket and check the HUD.
PCF8591 inputs always follow world north, east, south and west. A redstone connector instead lets you choose its own device-facing side.

entries.title: RAM and Flash map
entries.subtitle: 256-byte IDATA plus separate SFRs

blocks.text: The 256 bytes are the full indirect-addressable internal RAM, IDATA. The low half supports direct and indirect access; the upper half requires indirect addressing. Direct addresses 80H–FFH access SFRs, not the upper RAM bank.

MOV 80H,#00H ; writes P0 SFR
MOV R0,#80H
MOV @R0,#55H ; writes upper IDATA
SP resets to 07H and the stack grows upward. Check register-bank, variable and stack overlap in larger C projects. HEX validation rejects code exceeding 8 KiB.
XDATA versus I²C addresses >

entries.title: Common SFRs and interrupts
entries.subtitle: Control registers by address

blocks.text: Three interrupt checks

Enable the interrupt source, enable global EA, and return from the handler with RETI. Timers 0/1/2, external interrupts and UART use the implemented two-level IE/IP scheme. Do not depend on STC-specific extra sources or four-level priorities.

The interpreter supports all 255 defined base opcodes, bit operations, MOVC/MOVX, arithmetic and BCD adjustment. Watchdog, IAP/EEPROM and 6T/1T acceleration are not implemented; avoid requiring them in startup code.

entries.title: XDATA and bus addresses
entries.subtitle: Memory addresses and peripheral addresses

blocks.text: Since 1.10.1 no ADC, DAC or OLED is mapped into board memory. All 0000H–FFFFH, 64 KiB of XDATA, is ordinary emulator XRAM, separate from Flash, IDATA and SFR. It persists with CPU state. MOVX still reads and writes this RAM, which clears on reset or flashing.

MOV DPTR,#01234H
MOV A,#5AH
MOVX @DPTR,A ; store in XRAM
MOVX A,@DPTR ; read back 5AH
I²C addresses are not XDATA addresses

Writing XDATA 003CH does not reach OLED. I²C address 3CH is encoded as write byte 78H, followed by control 00H or 40H. OLED owns its 1024-byte RAM and consumes no MCU RAM window. A framebuffer allocated by firmware does consume MCU storage.
OLED I²C commands and pixel format >
External analog chip experiment >

entries.title: Software I²C
entries.subtitle: SDA/SCL can use any GPIO pair

blocks.text: I²C is driven by GPIO transitions and needs no separate hardware-I²C page. Choose two GPIOs labelled SDA and SCL and operate them in firmware. Release SDA by writing 1 before reading; a device pulls it low for 0 or ACK.

rows: SDA high-to-low while SCL is high
SDA low-to-high while SCL is high
MSB first; sample on rising SCL
Sender releases SDA; receiver ACKs or NACKs
Shift address left; add read bit

blocks.text: A seven-bit address differs from the byte on the bus. Shifting 48H left gives write 90H; setting bit 0 gives read 91H. Shifting 90H again targets the wrong address.

Different devices sharing SDA/SCL need unique addresses. The wiring page reports conflicts. I²C follows each MCU GPIO write and can complete inside one game tick; redstone world updates still occur by tick.

START/STOP, repeated START, addresses and ACK/NACK are supported. Analog voltage, multi-master arbitration and clock stretching are not simulated. SSD1306 scroll commands are accepted but currently do not animate scrolling.

entries.title: 1-Wire and temperature data
entries.subtitle: Reset, presence and CRC8

blocks.text: Standard-speed 1-Wire uses DQ. The controller holds low for at least 480 μs and releases. The probe gives a low presence pulse about 30–150 μs later. Each data slot begins low, then releases at the appropriate write/read time.
One measurement sequence
Reset, CC, 44, wait for conversion, reset, CC, BE, then read nine bytes. A 12-bit conversion takes up to about 750 ms; lower resolutions finish sooner. All bytes transfer LSB first.

CRC uses reflected Dallas polynomial 8CH over the first eight bytes and must match byte nine. Combine temperature low/high bytes as a signed number; at default 12-bit resolution divide by 16 for Celsius.
External power is implicit, so parasite-power strong pull-up is unnecessary. DQ still must be released before reads; holding it low prevents presence and data detection.

blocks.text: Share a sensor bus with OLED

All five sensor display programs use 12 MHz / 12T. OLED is at seven-bit 3CH on P1.6 SDA / P1.7 SCL. Branch the same group to the sensor and screen using a relay, or reuse the same GPIO pair on another face. DS18B20 uses a separate P1.2 DQ group; OLED stays on P1.6/P1.7.
Environment and PCF8591 both default to 48H: build these examples separately. MPU6050 firmware expects 68H; update its source if using 69H. OLED occupies no MCU memory window.
Live data, faults and recovery

Sensor demos continuously refresh and pad text to erase old digits, preserving negative temperatures. A missing sensor shows SENSOR OFFLINE; DS18B20 shows OFFLINE / CRC ERROR. Invalid readings are not presented as current data. Reconnecting the sensor or OLED automatically retries and restores display.

Environment shows redstone, sky/block light and day progress; PCF8591 shows four 0–255 ADC values and DAC; DS18B20 shows Celsius and CRC; MPU6050 shows acceleration in mg and angular rate in degrees/s; ALT-01 shows absolute, relative and zero height in cm and vertical speed in cm/s, without resetting its saved zero.
Sources and rebuilding

Complete C sources live in examples, with sensor_display.c/.h and protocol drivers in examples/drivers. tools/build-sensor-examples.ps1 uses SDCC SMALL, stack-auto and its matching library, limited to 8 KiB Flash and 256 B IDATA with no XDATA. Every source in the DS18B20 display project uses ED_DQ_BIT_ADDRESS=0x92; the generic appendix driver defaults to P3.7.

The SDCC script reserves DATA 30H–3FH for debug variables: environment/PCF8591 sample at 30H; DS18B20 scratchpad at 30H–38H and status A5H success/E1H error at 3FH. Configure Keil memory allocation and calling conventions separately; these new HEX files were compiled and executed with SDCC, not validated with Keil.

entries.title: Machines and temperature sources
entries.subtitle: Redstone, heat capabilities and estimates

blocks.text: Control machines with redstone

Redstone connectors work with technology components accepting vanilla redstone, such as Create clutches and links. Check the target component behavior before using GPIO for digital control or PCF8591 AOUT for analog output. The board does not directly rewrite Create rotational speed.
Where DS18B20 readings come from

rows: Controller heat converted by a game model
Biome model or provided temperature capability

blocks.text: Create heat levels are not native Celsius. Active heat levels 0–18 map to 20+5*level °C, passive heating to 60 °C and no heat to 20 °C. The probe explicitly labels this as Create heat conversion.

The probe still clamps to -55 to 125 °C and marks overrange. Other temperature mods are not universally detected: they need the embeddeddev:temperature capability or the corresponding provider interface.
Technology mods are optional. Boards, GPIO buses, electronics and vanilla temperature models remain usable without them.

entries.title: Appendix: complete copyable drivers
entries.subtitle: 11 driver groups; copy each .h, .c and minimal main

blocks.text: Code is read verbatim from examples/drivers when the handbook is generated. Each Copy button copies the entire file. Each driver includes its header, implementation and complete main demo; copy shared dependencies once.
Defaults use 12 MHz / 12T, especially DS18B20 short-slot sampling. Install a 12 MHz crystal, or adjust ED_FOSC_HZ and short delays first. Configured GPIO labels and pin numbers must match.

Keil C51: create an 8051 SMALL-model project, add the required .c files and one demo main, and add the header directory to Include Path. SDCC: compile each .c with -c into .rel, then link with main.c. Do not add every module to one 8 KiB project. Actual validation uses SDCC; the C51 declarations have not been verified with the Keil compiler.

I²C and most chip functions return 1 for success, 0 for NACK/CRC/invalid arguments. Do not use stale samples after failure. 1-Wire and 3-wire are separate protocols. Drivers use ordinary program memory/RAM, reserving no mapped peripheral window.

entries.title: Source: platform, delay and software I2C
entries.subtitle: Shared header and complete transport

blocks.text: Every project needs ed_platform.h. I²C drivers also need i2c_bus.h/.c; DS18B20 needs ed_delay.h/.c. ed_delay owns Timer0 and disables ET0; use Timer1/2 for other timing. Software I²C checks ACK and issues STOP on errors. Hardware clock stretching is not implemented.

The display owns all of P2, conflicting with default key9 on P2.0. RTC P3.0/P3.1 conflict with UART. Demos are independent. For a combined project, edit this header and configure matching block pins first.
